moving.title: Moving YEC between address types
moving.lede: A Ycash wallet holds YEC at three kinds of address: transparent ECC (`s1…` on mainnet), shielded Sapling (`ys1…`) and post-quantum (`sq…`, in two signature schemes, SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s and FN-DSA-512). This page says which call moves YEC from each to each, where the change goes, how to fund a vault from each, and how to read the balance of each, on every Ycash node line. It describes this release and later ones; 6.22.0-beta1 could not move YEC between Sapling and post-quantum addresses and did not split balances by type. The decisions it names (D-2 to D-9) are recorded in `docs/plans/yellowback-address-interop-plan.md` in this site's repository.

sections.title: ycashd 6.22 (ycash6, the release line)
sections.source: merged on ycash6 upgrade/vault: #96 balances, #98 getnewaddress, #99 sends, #100 vault_lock from (2026-11-11)
paragraphs: `z_sendmany` is the call that moves YEC between any two types (decision D-2). `sendtoaddress` and `sendmany` spend the wallet's transparent coins and pay ECC and post-quantum addresses.

**Privacy policy** (the fifth argument of `z_sendmany`, D-5): a post-quantum address counts as a transparent party, exactly as an ECC address does. With the default, `LegacyCompat`, every cell below is allowed. With a stricter policy, Sapling → post-quantum needs `AllowRevealedRecipients`; post-quantum → Sapling needs `AllowRevealedSenders`, or `AllowFullyTransparent` when the send has change (the change is a transparent output). A refusal is the node's usual `The specified privacy policy, …` message.

tables.caption: Send
rows: a new transparent address of the wallet
a Sapling note to the source address
`z_sendmany` from the address. `sendtoaddress` and `sendmany` may also spend post-quantum coins: they choose from all the wallet's transparent coins, so you cannot name the source
the source address (D-4: same scheme, no new key to back up); change below the post-quantum dust threshold joins the fee
notes: `z_mergetoaddress` takes the same address types: named ECC, Sapling and post-quantum sources (at most 100 post-quantum inputs per call; `ANY_TADDR` merges ECC coins only) into one ECC, Sapling or post-quantum address. `z_shieldcoinbase` refuses a post-quantum source, and a node refuses to start with a post-quantum `-mineraddress`.

A post-quantum send is priced on its size: about 27,000 zat for one SLH-DSA input and 5,500 for one FN-DSA-512 input. The default fee is raised to that price, and an explicit fee below it is refused. A post-quantum address can be spent from only once the vault upgrade is active at the next block, and an FN-DSA-512 (scheme 2) address only once Falcon is active as well. The wallet must be unlocked.
A post-quantum address is transparent. Paying one from Sapling reveals the amount and the recipient, as paying an ECC address does.

paragraphs: kogany has no wallet. It validates, relays and mines transactions; for the mixed shapes this is tested on a chain recorded on a C++ line and replayed into kogany (kogany#17: Sapling spends and outputs beside post-quantum and vault scripts, with negative controls). Still open: an FN-DSA input beside a Sapling spend, a vault unlock beside Sapling parts, and reject-reason parity with both C++ lines. The wallet of the kogany product is `yewd`, a separate process that answers the wallet RPCs.
yewd does not serve `z_gettotalbalance`, `listaddresses` or `z_mergetoaddress` (it answers only the post-quantum refusals of `z_mergetoaddress` and `z_shieldcoinbase`).

sections.title: Which scheme is this address?
sections.pending: D-9 prefix pair ycash-dd #166 / ycash6 #95 (and kogany, yew, the clients) not merged on any line (2026-11-11)
sections.pendingText: Scheme-visible prefixes come with the release that carries decision D-9 (RPC contract version 9). Until then both schemes share one prefix and only `validateaddress` (`pqscheme`) or the listings above tell them apart.
paragraphs: From the release that carries D-9, a post-quantum address shows its scheme in the third character: `f` for FN-DSA-512 (Falcon), `s` for SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s. Each prefix is one 3-byte Base58Check version, so the address stays 53 characters (3-byte version, 32-byte key hash, checksum). The ECC YED address is unchanged: 35 characters, `yb…` on mainnet.

A binary without D-9 (6.22.0-beta1 among them) writes the older 53-character form with no scheme letter (`sq…`, `tq…`, `rq…` for YEC; `yb…`, `yt…`, `yr…` for YED; on testnet both schemes begin `tq3`) and refuses an address in the new form as invalid. A binary with D-9 refuses the older form, except when it loads its own address book or a key dump written before D-9. `yed_getinfo.params.pqAddressVersion` and `.params.pq.plainAddressVersion` become objects keyed by scheme number.

unavailable.title: Not available on Ycash
unavailable.reason: Unified-address accounts need the NU5 network upgrade. NU5 has no activation height on any Ycash network, so the node refuses this call: "Unified-address accounts require the NU5 network upgrade, which is not active on Ycash."
